posthoc_raw_bitmap_scanner_sensitivity.model: one raw96 beat inspected per cycle; a nonzero descriptor is available in its discovery cycle; EOT is available after the fixed token extent; no additional compactor, FIFO, SRAM, or wire delay
posthoc_raw_bitmap_scanner_sensitivity.interpretation: optimistic latency lower bound for a posthoc scanner, not a physical implementation
posthoc_raw_bitmap_scanner_sensitivity.finding: zero-beat elision is not a latency win when generated by a serialized posthoc raw-bitmap scan; the reported indexed advantage requires a native event tap or a prebuilt sparse index

P0: Implement and exact-payload-miter either an ATLIF-native indexed event tap or a prebuilt sparse-index memory. A serialized posthoc raw96 scanner has an optimistic K4 lower bound of 159902252 cycles, 1.522 percent slower than raw96, so it cannot supply the M176 speedup.

Compose the indexed producer, a finite ready/valid descriptor buffer, and the corrected five-bit beat-index frontend in VCS/DC; validate 120-payload descriptor conservation, index extent, EOT/backpressure, same-cycle re-arm, and producer stalls before admitting the analytic latency sums as executable.
Compose explicit four-bank weight response, M169 arithmetic, accumulator context, and final commit with the frontend before making any complete-FC2 or physical speedup claim.
P1: Seal a terminology correction overlay because the immutable M176 analyzer/result still say absolute base-row while the current README/contract correctly specify a five-bit absolute beat index reconstructed as index times twelve; numerical counts are unaffected but evidence wording is split.

Specify and synthesize the descriptor encoding and memory word. The count reduction is 32.979 percent, but an illustrative 102-bit descriptor reduces bits by 28.790 percent and 128-bit alignment reduces them by only 10.638 percent.
Run matched raw96, raw128, and indexed96 RTL plus DC with identical source, FIFO, tag, SRAM, and output backpressure assumptions; analytic raw128 versus indexed96 is not a physical A/B.
Recompute the indexed population and bank pressure after the final PAFT checkpoint, because M176 is frozen ep35 only.
Expand beyond ten samples and report per-sequence and per-token tail latency, especially the 1863944 all-zero tokens and gaps as long as 30 beats.
Measure memory and compactor energy; even a fully hidden producer scan may erase the energy benefit unless indexing is generated natively at ATLIF write time.
P2: Add the release-aware posthoc scanner sensitivity as a first-class production DSE point instead of leaving producer cost only in prose claim boundaries.
Report descriptor count, payload bits, sideband bits, aligned storage bits, and accepted cycles separately; avoid saying 25 percent lower width without naming whether sideband is included.

Materialize at least one exact indexed descriptor trace with beat indices and EOT markers so monotonicity, extent, order, and exactly-once event preservation are checked on an actual transport artifact rather than inferred positions.
recommended_next_step: Keep M176 as a valid analytic opportunity result, but make the native ATLIF-indexed producer the architecture. Do not implement a posthoc raw bitmap scanner as the claimed acceleration path; first seal producer plus finite FIFO plus corrected indexed frontend, then attach weight memory and M169.
